This plant belongs to the same family as the rose.
rarely: He rarely eats meat, preferring vegetables and grains instead.
voice: the sound produced when speaking or singing; a viewpoint expressed
The rights are real, but the voice speaking for them is borrowed.
agreed: settled or decided by mutual consent
The agreed price included delivery and installation costs.
boom: a period of rapid growth or increase
The city experienced a housing boom during the past decade.
left: remaining after others have gone or been used
Only a few seats were left by the time we arrived.
marks: shows or indicates something, or makes a visible sign on it
A small star marks the correct answer on the page.
land: the solid part of the earth's surface, as opposed to sea or air
Coral reefs help protect the land from strong ocean waves.
rush: a busy period with much activity or heavy traffic
giờ cao điểm; sự vội vã
Traffic barely moves during the evening rush.
forests: large areas covered mainly with trees
Tropical forests are home to an enormous variety of species.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
cleared: settled or paid off completely, especially a debt
The loan was finally cleared after ten years of payments.
pump: to move liquid or gas using a machine or force
Farmers pump water from the river to irrigate their fields.
large: A large crowd gathered outside the stadium before the match.
amounts: The farm produces large amounts of fresh vegetables every single week.
groundwater: water held underground in soil or rock
The village relies on groundwater pumped from a deep well.
water: the clear liquid needed for life, found in rivers and seas
Soil and grass hold water, and as it evaporates it carries heat away.
dry: Make sure the paint is completely dry before touching it.
season: one of the main periods of the year, or a period of a particular activity
Mango season brings extra income to farmers each year.
drought: a long period of unusually low rainfall
The region suffered a severe drought that damaged most of the crops.
wells: deep holes dug to reach underground water
Thousands of wells take water from the same underground layers.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
low: not high in level, amount or position
Prices stayed low throughout most of the summer.
hotter: having a higher temperature; comparative of hot
This summer has been noticeably hotter than last year's.
climate: the general weather conditions typical of an area over a long period
The region has a mild climate with cool, wet winters.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
parts: pieces or components that make up something
The mechanic replaced several worn parts inside the old engine.
suitable: right or appropriate for a particular purpose
This film is not suitable for young children.
future: the period of time that is to come
Nobody can predict exactly what the future holds.
shade: a particular version of a colour
She chose a darker shade of blue for the bedroom walls.
carefully: in a way that shows care and attention to detail
He carefully wrapped the fragile plates before packing the box.
protecting: The soldiers were protecting the border village from further attacks.
nature: the basic or inherent character of a person or thing; the physical world
It is human nature to notice bad news more than good news.
business: a particular task, activity, or matter to be dealt with
Organizing the wedding turned into a stressful business for everyone involved.
trying: present participle of try; making an attempt to do something
Closing the book and trying to write the same content from memory feels far worse but works far better.
different: not the same as another or each other
Every student in the class has a different learning style.
path: a route or track made for people to walk along
They followed a narrow path through the woods to the lake.
speciality: a particular product, subject, or skill someone is known for
Seafood pasta is the restaurant's speciality.
instead: He skipped dinner and had a light snack instead.
selling: giving something to someone in exchange for money
The company earns most of its income from selling software licences.
alone: without other people or things present
He prefers to travel alone rather than join a large tour group.
pick: to choose or gather something carefully
Let the children pick their own fruit at the orchard.
ripe: fully grown and ready to be eaten
She picked only the ripe tomatoes from the vine.
batch: a quantity of something produced or handled at one time
The bakery sells out of its first batch of croissants by nine o'clock.
separate: not joined or connected; existing apart
The twins prefer to have separate bedrooms now.
be: to exist, or to have a particular state or quality
It can be difficult to stay calm during an emergency.
traced: past tense of trace; followed something back to its origin
They keep each batch separate so its origin can be traced.
buyers: plural of buyer; people or organizations that purchase goods
Foreign buyers are showing renewed interest in the local property market.
care: serious attention or caution applied to a task
Handle the antique vase with great care while moving it.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
flavour: the distinctive taste of a food or drink
Adding lemon juice gives the soup a fresh flavour.
such: of the type already mentioned or described
Such behaviour will not be tolerated in the workplace.
long: having a great length or duration
It was a long journey across three different countries.
dismissed: rejected or refused to consider seriously
Her concerns were dismissed by the committee without discussion.
cheap: Street food here is cheap and surprisingly delicious.
harsh: The desert has a harsh climate with little rainfall.
processed: treated or prepared through a series of manufacturing steps
Highly processed foods often contain more salt and sugar than fresh ones.
fine: Don't worry about the delay, it's fine with me.
changing: The climate is changing faster in polar regions than elsewhere.
reputation: the general opinion people hold about someone or something
The restaurant built its reputation on fresh, local ingredients.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
easy: The test was easy enough that most students finished early.
needs: The garden needs watering twice a week during summer.
labour: physical or mental work, especially hard work
Harvesting the crop by hand requires a great deal of labour.
careful: giving serious attention to avoiding mistakes or harm
A careful reading of the contract revealed a hidden fee.
premium: of high quality and higher price than usual
The store sells premium coffee beans imported directly from small farms.
market: a place or system where goods are bought and sold
Farmers bring fresh produce to the market every morning.
still: continuing to be the case; even more so
Despite the rain, the match still went ahead as planned.
compared: examined alongside something else to note similarities or differences
The results were compared with those from an earlier study.
trade: the buying and selling of goods and services
A map of those names traces a trade network more accurately than most surviving records.
ordinary: normal or usual; not special or different
For most families, an ordinary weekend involves chores and errands.
manage: to succeed in doing something difficult; to control or direct
She had to manage a busy restaurant on her own that night.
reward: something given in return for good behaviour or effort
Finishing the marathon felt like a reward in itself.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
control: the power to direct or influence something
The pilot regained control of the aircraft after a tense few seconds.
